Spiritborn · Meta

Evade Counterswarm Spiritborn

mobility-driven poison swarm

Spiritborn meta unchanged mobility-driven poison swarm

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

The best speed-farming build in the game this season and the only non-Barbarian build Maxroll rates S on both its overall endgame list and its push list. The name is slightly misleading in a way worth fixing up front: the damage is not the Evade. It comes from Pestilent Swarms created by Counterattack running the Lord of Hatred variant Counterattack of the Swarm, and Rushing Claw - with the Evasive Swipe variant, which dashes without needing a target - is used purely as a movement skill. You hold it down and the swarms orbiting you grind through everything you pass. The guide is explicit that Rushing Claw 'doesn't actually count as an Evade, so you can't use Cem', and the whole gearing problem follows from that: every cooldown affix on rings, gloves, helm and amulet exists to shorten Rushing Claw's charge cooldown. Two hard prerequisites: Ring of Writhing Moon, to keep the swarms circling you, and the Prodigy's Tempo paragon board and its legendary node. Because the damage is a damage-over-time, critical strikes cannot crit it, so crit chance is carried only far enough to proc Widow's Web - a genuinely inverted stat priority worth knowing before you gear. The honest counterweight to the S ratings: TierListHQ holds the class at A, 'great at speed, weak at bossing', and this build only partly answers that through Scourge triggering the five-piece set on single targets. And three separate bug situations touch it, which must not be run together. The build deliberately uses one - 'you use Tzic for the 6x damage bug on unstoppable enemies and bosses'. A second constrains it: a Spirit tag inheritance bug means charm +Ranks do not work through Lord of Hatred skill variants, which is why the Berú of Kwatli's Grace set is unusable in most variants; the developers have acknowledged it and a fix missed the Season 14 launch. A third makes Harmony of Ebewaka occasionally drop Ravager below its four-rank minimum. Separately, the Poison Stinger bug in Maxroll's week-1 article belongs to a different Spiritborn build and is not this one's.

Requirements

  • Ring of Writhing Moonring 1
  • Loyalty's Mantlehelm
  • Harmony of Ebewakahelm
  • Widow's Webamulet
Stage
Move on whenLoyalty's Mantle in the helm slot. Until then cooldown reduction is a scavenger hunt across rings, gloves, helm and amulet; once it is a crafted Mythic the guide says you no longer need cooldown affixes or tempers at all.
Move on when30+ ranks in Ravager. That is the guide's stated requirement for Rushing Claw's Evolving Claws variant, which refills charges permanently from Ferocity - and it is what the next stage is built on.
Move on whenMythic-tier gear plus a Mythic Talisman seal. At that point the choice is Push for Pit and Tower depth or the Speedfarm branch for sub-two-minute Torment 12 clears - a fork, not a further step.

Rotation

The guide's own order: activate all the secondary cooldowns - Ravager, Toxic Skin, Scourge and The Devourer - then cast both charges of Counterattack to spin up the swarms, then spam Rushing Claw. Keep refreshing cooldowns as soon as they are up. Expect friction early: 'sometimes Rushing Claw will still be on cooldown and then you will need to run & normal evade for movement while waiting'.

Skill point priority

  1. Scope note: this is an endgame-only guide - 'use one of our Spiritborn leveling guides to knock out the prerequisites for this build and get started' - so this stage records its Starter variant, a level-70 Torment-1 entry point, not a 1-70 route. The guide links Rock Splitter Thorns and Stinger as the levelling builds it does endorse
  2. Counterattack first: it is the damage, and you want both charges online
  3. Rushing Claw next - this is your movement and therefore your uptime
  4. Ravager, which feeds Ferocity and later gates the Evolving Claws swap at 30+ ranks
  5. Scourge absorbs spare points: 'any remaining skill points you get from the Season Journey can be put into Scourge for more damage'
  6. Invest in Vortex and Concussive Stomp even though neither is on the bar - Vortex fires from the Kry rune, Concussive Stomp from Tzic
  7. Do not chase critical strike chance: 'Critical Strikes aren't required because Damage over Time (DoT) can't crit'

Skill point priority

  1. This stage records the guide's Midgame_Easy variant, which is the path it actually recommends: 'most will find that the most natural progression for variants with this build is: Starter -> Midgame_Easy -> Endgame_Hard -> Push'. Easy and Hard are gearing requirements, not power levels - the Easy variants 'take shortcuts with cooldown reduction to make it easier to play'
  2. Counterattack stays maxed; it remains the sole damage engine
  3. Rushing Claw still on Evasive Swipe here, so it dashes whether or not there is a target
  4. Ravager climbing toward the 30-rank gate that unlocks the next stage's Evolving Claws swap
  5. Scourge continues to take spare Season Journey points, and is also the Vulnerable source
  6. Toxic Skin for sustain - healing in this build comes from Toxic Skin and The Devourer, nothing else
  7. Spirit Halls flip to Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary here, and it is mandatory rather than optimal: Loyalty's Mantle requires it because of the Spirit tag inheritance bug

Skill point priority

  1. This stage records Endgame_Hard, the guide's recommended endgame: 'focused more on damage and less on cooldowns, since you can refill your Rushing Claw charges'
  2. Hard requirement, in the guide's own capitals: you must have 30+ ranks in Ravager to run Rushing Claw's Evolving Claws variant for permanent charge refill from Ferocity
  3. Know the cost of that swap: Evolving Claws requires enemy targets to cast at, 'so you will need to run normally when there aren't targets around'

  6. Charm ranks must match your primary Spirit Hall - 'make sure any ranks you have from charms align to your primary/main spirit hall to avoid this issue', the issue being the inheritance bug

Skill point priority

  1. The guide's own change list for Push: drop the Prodigy's Tempo board for Bitter Medicine, swap Loyalty's Mantle for Harmony of Ebewaka and the Spirit Halls to Gorilla main and Eagle secondary, run Tzic for the 6x damage bug on unstoppable enemies and bosses, and run Rushing Claw on Evolving Claws for the Ferocity refill
  2. Exploiter's Aspect goes on the boots - it does not apply to bosses, but it pushes elites into Unstoppable, which is what lets Tzic do its work
  3. 30+ Ravager ranks is non-negotiable here
  4. Cast The Devourer the moment it is off cooldown: 'its important to cast your Ultimate as soon as it is off cooldown to ramp this up'
  5. Scourge for Vulnerable and for triggering the five-piece set on single targets, which is this build's partial answer to the class's bossing weakness
  6. Survivability floor from the guide's own changelog: 'it is not recommended to be below 38k life, if you are pushing for the highest content'

Board & glyph focus

Glyph level order, published as an ordered list and identical in every variant: Consumption, Canny, Fester, Bane, Menagerist. The board strategy is a rush - 'one of the most efficient strategies is to rush to get your Legendary nodes even before you slot in glyphs. You will obtain the power spike from these faster than you will focusing on glyphs'. Prodigy's Tempo is the named build-requirement board at this stage. Spirit Halls here are Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary; Gorilla primary is one of the two Barrier sources, alongside the Tzic rune. Do not use the Colossal glyph - the guide removed it after finding it does not work properly with the swarm's damage-over-time.

How to run them

Identical across all eight of the guide's variants, and quoted almost verbatim: hire Subo 'for his map hacks and increased damage from Scorched Earth & Incendiary Bolt', reinforce with Raheir's Bastion 'for additional DR & Unstoppable'. The map visibility is not a luxury on a build whose entire point is crossing a map as fast as possible, and Bastion is doing the survivability work that a build with no defensive skill on the bar cannot do for itself.

Uniques & where to find them

Ring of Writhing Moonring 1

Target-farm Lord Zir. This is a hard prerequisite, not an upgrade - it is what keeps the swarms circling you rather than left behind. The guide rates it 'your lowest priority in upgrading to a mythic unique', so take the plain Unique and spend your Mythic on the helm instead.

Where →
Loyalty's Mantlehelm

Target-farm Bartuc. The guide's designated crafted Mythic: 'once you have this as a crafted mythic, you no longer need Cooldown affixes or Tempers', which is the single biggest gearing simplification in the build. Note the string attached - it locks you to Jaguar primary and Jaguar secondary Spirit Halls because of the Spirit tag inheritance bug.

Where →
Harmony of Ebewakahelm

Target-farm Bartuc. Replaces Loyalty's Mantle at the late endgame and for pushing, which also flips the Spirit Halls to Gorilla primary and Eagle secondary. Carries a known bug: granted skill ranks based on the secondary Spirit Hall occasionally cause Ravager to lose its four-rank minimum when you are at 30 ranks.

Where →
Widow's Webamulet

Target-farm Duriel. Taken for extra AoE damage, and it is the only reason this build carries any critical strike chance at all. It does not combine with Shattered Vow - the guide says plainly 'they don't work together'.

Where →

Loot filter

Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter (in-guide import code)

maxroll.gg

The guide ships its own filter by name - 'Ignition's Swarms 2.3 Loot Filter' - as an import code in its Loot Filter section, with sub-toggles including 'HIDE Glaive & QStaff', which matters because this build wants a Polearm specifically. That is the exact match. A name-matching community mirror exists at https://diablo4lootfilter.com/filters/evade-counterswarm-spiritborn-loot-filter-code, but it is a third-party copy that may lag version 2.3 and was confirmed only through search metadata, not by loading the page - prefer the in-guide code.
